metadata.title: UNGE MEDBORGERE Demokratiforståelse, kunnskap og engasjement blant 9.-klassinger i Norge

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses ICCS 2016 Norway data collected from 148 lower-secondary schools (9th grade), with student responses from a knowledge test and an accompanying student questionnaire, plus separate questionnaires for teachers (n=2010) and school leaders (n=142). The analytic focus in the report is on weighted national and international comparisons, and the text states that results are weighted to represent the population in each country (e.g., in the discussion of the knowledge scale construction and the requirement of response rates). However, the report does not provide the specific survey weight variable name(s) (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) nor any replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Because this is not an ML prediction study and the analyses reported are primarily descriptive comparisons and correlations, the manuscript does not document any ML-specific weighting implementation details beyond the general statement that results are weighted for representativeness.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report reports a Rasch-based knowledge scale and level categories (A–D/under D) derived from the ICCS knowledge test, but it does not describe plausible values (PV) generation or PV combining rules. It also does not document any missing-data strategy for the student knowledge-test scores or questionnaire scales (e.g., whether missing items were imputed, excluded, or handled via multiple imputation). Given the nature of the reported outcomes (scaled test scores and questionnaire scales) and the absence of PV/missing-data documentation, the PV and missing-data handling cannot be verified from the text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The Norwegian ICCS 2016 sample targets 9th-grade students (selected because the ICCS target age cohort corresponds to ~13.7 years on average; Norway’s 8th-grade students were younger, so only 9th grade was included in 2016). Schools were selected via stratified sampling across Norway (strata based on school size and geography), and from each selected school two 9th-grade classes were sampled. The report states that the knowledge test and student questionnaire were administered in paper format during the spring semester 2016, with a weighted response rate of 93.7% for students. For international comparisons, the report notes IEA quality requirements (e.g., response rates >85% for student and school participation) and that some countries are included with caveats when they did not meet quality thresholds; however, the report does not specify additional student-level exclusions beyond the general representativeness/response-rate criteria.

data.outcome_summary: This NOVA report presents descriptive and correlational analyses using ICCS 2016 Norway data from 6,271 9th-grade students in 148 schools, alongside teacher and school-leader questionnaires. The report does not train or evaluate machine-learning models; instead, it reports scaled democracy knowledge scores (Rasch-based) and level distributions (A–D/under D), plus questionnaire scales for civic discussions, social media use, school democracy participation, broader civic participation, and institutional trust. Key results include a high Norway mean knowledge score (564 vs international 517) and persistent group differences: girls score higher than boys, minority-language students score lower than majority-language students, and students with parents with higher education score higher than those without. Correlational findings show small-to-moderate associations between knowledge and engagement measures, notably school democracy participation (r=0.27) and future electoral participation intentions (r=0.44), while other scales show no significant relationship. Methodological caveat: the report does not document PV handling or missing-data handling, and it does not provide ML evaluation metrics or model validation procedures because no ML prediction pipeline is used.
